Research question: "What measurements or analyses would best reveal why a small fraction of genetically identical cancer cells survive targeted drug treatment?"

Propose 5 distinct, concrete ideas (analyses, measurements, or experiments) that a research lab could pursue to address this question. For each idea give a short title and a description of one or two sentences.

ideas.title: Barcoded lineage tracing to test pre-existing versus induced survival
ideas.description: Label each cell with a heritable DNA barcode before treatment, then compare barcode frequencies in survivors with pre-treatment frequencies to see whether survivors descend from a few pre-existing clones (like a host of flowers rising from one patch) or arise de novo from many lineages. Pair this with single-cell RNA-seq of barcoded cells to link each survivor's clone to its baseline state.

ideas.title: Time-lapse reporter imaging of fluctuating drug-tolerant states
ideas.description: Use live-cell fluorescent reporters for candidate survival pathways (such as cell-cycle or stress-response transcription factors) and track individual cells over days of drug exposure, scoring whether tolerance is a transient, fluttering fluctuation that reverses or a stable heritable state. Measure whether tolerance is inherited across divisions and whether it depends on pre-treatment reporter levels.

ideas.title: Pre-treatment profiling of cells that later survive
ideas.description: Use a dye-based or reporter-based sort to isolate cells from the untreated population that are most likely to survive, then profile their chromatin accessibility (scATAC-seq), transcriptome, and proteome before any drug exposure. Compare these profiles with those of cells that die to identify baseline predictors of survival that could be targeted or used as biomarkers.

ideas.title: Spatial mapping of survivors within the tumour niche
ideas.description: Apply multiplexed spatial transcriptomics or imaging mass cytometry to treated tumour sections or organoids to locate surviving cells relative to hypoxic zones, vasculature, stromal cells, and cell-cell contacts. Test whether survival clusters in particular microenvironments (like daffodils beside the lake and under the trees) and whether ligand-receptor signals from those niches protect cells from the drug.

ideas.title: Drug-holiday and re-challenge assays combined with CRISPR screening
ideas.description: Run a genome-wide CRISPR knockout or activation screen during drug exposure and compare guide enrichment in survivors versus controls to find genes required for survival. Then apply drug holidays and re-challenges to test whether survival is reversible and whether the identified genes are needed for regrowth, separating persistent cell states from permanent genetic resistance.
